subject: Pricing clarification: VPC deployment fee structure and operator-license tradeoffs
messages:
From: Dana Lee <procurement@novamed.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Pricing clarification: VPC deployment fee structure

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the draft quote. Before we present this to our finance committee next week we need a couple of clarifications so the numbers map back to our capital planning:

- Can you provide a simple side-by-side of platform fee amortization options (12/24/36 months) and the impact on quarterly spend?
- For operator licenses vs node-credit approach: what operational risk do you see if we choose operator-license (per-operator) instead of per-node credits? Specifically concerned about SRE headcount growth over time.
- We also need to understand the support tiers — response times, oncall coverage, and what is included in escalation vs billable professional services.

If possible, please attach the SOW and the fee model so our legal + procurement can run the numbers. Alex (cc'd) will review technical assumptions.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — committee packet closes Friday.

Best,
Dana Lee
Senior Procurement Manager
NovaMed

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Dana Lee <procurement@novamed.com>, Alex Park <sre-lead@novamed.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Pricing clarification: VPC deployment fee structure

Dana — thanks for the note and the tight timeline. Attached are the SOW and the fee workbook; below is a concise summary to include in your packet. Let me know if you want these as slides.

Summary (high level)
- Platform fee amortization: 12m = $1.35M upfront (no amortization), 24m = $750k/year (blended), 36m = $540k/year (lowest annualized cost). See tab "Amortization" in the workbook for quarterly impact.
- Operator-license vs node credit: operator-license is priced per named operator seat and is ideal when a small, stable ops team will run the deployment. Node-credits tie to capacity (GPU/node) and scale predictably with load. Risk tradeoffs: operator-license reduces variable cloud-like spend but risks under/over provisioning if SRE headcount changes; node credits reduce SRE headcount sensitivity but can lead to higher unit costs under low utilization. Attached comparison has a short risk matrix.
- Support tiers (Bronze / Silver / Gold):
  - Bronze: business-hours support, 24h response for Sev2, included incident guidance;
  - Silver: 24x7 coverage for Sev1/Sev2, 4h response for Sev1, on-call rotation, quarterly health checks;
  - Gold: 24x7 prioritized routing, 1h response Sev1, monthly operational reviews, two named escalation engineers and one on-prem handoff runbook.

Recommended starting config for NovaMed pilot
- 12-month pilot with 6 months of platform credits (applied to first invoice) to de-risk rollout
- Operator-license for up to 3 named operators during pilot, then switch to node-credits at scale (we can convert remaining credit balance)
- Silver support for production pilot; upgrade to Gold for enterprise SLA on go-live

Attachments: Novamed_Rollout_SOW_v1.pdf, platform_fee_model_v3.xlsx, operator_license_vs_node_credit_comparison.pdf

Irene and Marissa are looped in to confirm commercial flexibility — filing for a revised commercial offer now.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Mateo — thanks, that helps. A few follow-ups from finance and SRE:

- Finance asked if Redwood can provide a 25% discount on the platform fee for a 24-month commit (we're targeting a 2-year budget window). If not, what is the best you can do?
- For the operator-license approach: Alex is concerned about an explosion of named operators during ramp. Can we get a hard cap on operator seats for the first 12 months with a simple convert-to-node-credit formula if exceeded?
- SLA credits: can you confirm the formula for credits on missed availability (standard SLA credit tiers) and whether Gold includes a financial uptime guarantee?

We're trying to keep the ask constrained — committee wants an updated quote by EOD Thursday.

Thanks,
Dana

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Pricing clarification: VPC deployment fee structure and requested concessions

Forwarding NovaMed asks — finance is pushing for 25% off platform fee on 24m commit and SRE wants a hard cap on operator seats with a convert-to-node-credit fallback. Committee needs updated quote by EOD tomorrow.

Proposed commercial response (internal) — please reply with edits:
1) Platform fee discount
   - Offer: 20% discount on platform fee for a 24-month committed term (instead of 25%). Rationale: preserves unit economics and aligns with similar deals. Provide 6 months of platform credits applied to invoices as additional concession.
2) Operator-license cap and conversion formula
   - Offer: Hard cap of 4 named operator seats for months 0–12. If NovaMed needs more, excess seats are automatically converted at the prevailing node-credit rate with a 30-day notice and pro-rated credit against platform fee.
3) SLA & credits
   - Silver: no financial uptime guarantee but standard support credits for Sev1/Sev2 as in the SLA table.
   - Gold: 99.95% uptime financial SLA with credits tiered (0.1% = 5% credit, 0.5% = 15% credit, etc.). Legal to confirm exact wording; propose to include a 90-day remedy window.
4) Risk matrix note (to include in packet):
   - Operational growth risk: operator-seat mismatch -> mitigated by conversion formula
   - Cost predictability: platform fee amortized options provided
   - Escalation cadence: Gold tier includes named escalation engineers and runbook

If you approve I will send a clean revised quote to Dana and attach updated workbook showing the 20% discount and credit column.

Thanks — Mateo
